newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Chance of finding ski lodge survivors remote-police.
newsitem.headline: Chance of finding ski lodge survivors remote-police.

text.p: Hopes of finding survivors in the ruins of two lodges buried by a landslide at an Australian ski resort faded on Friday as rescuers continued the grim and dangerous task of digging through tonnes of rubble.
"I think at this stage the chances are quite remote," Assistant Commissioner Ken Moroney told reporters, but he added that rescuers had not given up all hope.
The body of a man, one of 20 people buried by Wednesday night's landslide at Thredbo Alpine Village in the Snowy Mountains, 400 km (250 miles) south of Sydney, was recovered overnight.
"We would hope to locate additional persons...and one can always entertain a degree of hope they will be alive," Moroney said.
"But...the nature of time and the nature of the weather probably allows us to entertain some degrgee of concern."
Rescuers using optic fibre cameras and thermal imaging equipment have found no signs of life in the wreckage of the Carinya and Bimbadeen lodges.
Relatives of the missing rushed to Thredbo and are being briefed by police and offered the help of grief counsellors.
A total of 500 emergency workers are now involved in the operation, sifting by hand through tonnes of soil, rock and trees, concrete and metal left in the wake of the landslide.

Efforts to search for the remaining 11 men and eight women remained painstakingly slow in the freezing conditions with the temperature falling to a low of minus 9 degrees Celsius (16 degrees Fahrenheit) overnight, forcing rescuers to operate in brief shifts.
Rescuers also have been forced to shore up the site as they work to prevent a further slide. "The area still remains unstable," a police spokeswoman told Reuters.
Police said the 20 trapped were a middle-aged couple from California, a New Zealand woman and 17 Australians. They did not identify the body already found.
Experts believe seepage from a mountain spring may have caused the earth to give way.

Witnesses said the landslide hit like a "tornado", sending the side of a mountain crashing into the Carinya lodge, which contained one person, and cascading onto the Bimbadeen lodge which had 18 people inside.
Despite initial frantic efforts by tourists to reach people crying out for help, police quickly halted rescue efforts for hours due to fears of more landslides.
The landslide occurred at the height of the Australian skiing season when Thredbo is packed with thousands of Australian and foreign visitors.
The village, at an altitude of 1,370 metres (4,494 feet), sits on a ridge facing the snow-covered mountain range of the Kosciuszko National Park.
